sources.name: GitHub issues of tailwindlabs/tailwindcss
sources.version: GitHub REST API 2022-11-28, state as of 2026-11-11
sources.license: GitHub Terms of Service (user content; only facts and our own summaries are kept)

provenance.notes: URL, number, title, state, dates, counts and labels are copied from the API response of each issue. Category, components, summary, resolution and lesson are written by the researcher (tools/extract/field-reports/curation) after reading the issue body returned by the search API and, for the issues listed in docs/research/field-reports.md, the full thread. daysOpen of an open issue is measured to the retrieval date. fixedBy is filled mechanically from merged pull requests that name the issue after a closing keyword. Reports marked needs-review state a cause that the researcher inferred from the symptom without a confirming statement in the issue.

reports.title: [Feature Proposal] Support CSS Logical Properties
reports.summary: In 2019 a contributor proposed utilities for CSS logical properties, pointing out that left/right in margin, padding and border only make sense for left-to-right horizontal writing. The proposal drew many reactions and was closed weeks later; logical utilities arrived in the framework years afterwards.
reports.lesson: Our utility and token names are logical from day one (inline-start/end), since later addition leaves an ecosystem of physical classes that then needs codemods.

reports.title: space-x-* does not work in RTL direction
reports.summary: The space-between utilities add a margin on a fixed physical side of every child but the first, so under RTL the gap lands on the wrong side: one item touches its neighbour and an extra gap appears at the edge.
reports.lesson: Spacing between siblings is done with gap, never with per-child physical margins.

reports.title: rtl language support when using dir=rtl
reports.summary: With dir="rtl", the first space between elements was missing when using the space-between utilities; the report, like several near-identical ones over three years, was closed by pointing to a manual reverse modifier that authors must add per direction.
reports.lesson: A layout primitive must not need a per-direction modifier from the author; Stack and Group use gap.

reports.title: divide not exactly between flex box sub items in RTL language
reports.summary: Divider utilities draw a border on a fixed physical side of each child, so in an RTL flex row the dividers do not fall between the items.
reports.lesson: Separators between items are drawn with logical borders (border-inline-start on every item but the first) or as separate elements.

reports.title: ltr and rtl don't respect the direction when dir=auto is used
reports.summary: The rtl: and ltr: variants match on an ancestor's dir attribute value, so they do not apply inside dir="auto", where the browser resolves the direction from the content.
reports.lesson: Direction-dependent styles rely on logical properties and the :dir() pseudo-class, which follow the resolved direction, not on [dir=rtl] attribute selectors; dir="auto" content is a fixture.
